'''Emanuel Parzen''' (April 21, 1929 – February 6, 2016) was an American [[statistician]]. He worked and published on [[signal detection theory]] and [[time series]] analysis, where he pioneered the use of [[kernel density estimation]] (also known as the [[Parzen window]]<ref name="parzen_1962">{{Cite journal | last1 = Parzen | first1 = E. | author-link = Emanuel Parzen| title = On Estimation of a Probability Density Function and Mode | doi = 10.1214/aoms/1177704472 | journal = [[The Annals of Mathematical Statistics]]| volume = 33 | issue = 3 | pages = 1065–1076 | year = 1962 | jstor = 2237880| url = http://dml.cz/bitstream/handle/10338.dmlcz/140760/Kybernetika_46-2010-3_10.pdf | doi-access = free }}</ref> in his honor). Parzen was the recipient of the 1994 [[Samuel Stanley Wilks|Samuel S. Wilks]] Memorial Medal of the [[American Statistical Association]].<ref name="newton_2002">{{Cite journal | last1 = Newton | first1 = H. Joseph| title = A Conversation with Emanuel Parzen | doi = 10.1214/ss/1042727944 | journal = [[Statistical Science]]| volume = 17 | issue = 3 | pages = 357–378| year = 2002 | jstor = 3182796| doi-access = free}}</ref>

==Biography==

Parzen attended [[Bronx High School of Science]]. He then matriculated to [[Harvard University|Harvard]], where he earned his undergraduate degree in mathematics in 1949. From there, he went on to [[University of California, Berkeley|Berkeley]], earning his master and doctorate degrees in mathematics in 1951 and 1953, respectively. His dissertation, "On Uniform Convergence of Families of Sequences of Random Variables", was written under [[Michel Loève]].

Parzen went directly into academia after graduate school, first serving as a research scientist in the physics department and assistant professor of mathematical statistics at [[Columbia University]]. He left there in 1956 for [[Stanford University]], where he stayed for the next 14 years. During this time, he wrote what has become one of the classical texts in probability theory.<ref name="parzen_1960">Parzen, E. (1960) ''Modern Probability Theory and Its Applications'', John Wiley and Sons, New York.</ref> In 1970, he accepted the chair of the statistics department at [[University at Buffalo, The State University of New York|SUNY Buffalo]] and in 1978 moved to his last post as a Distinguished Professor at [[Texas A&M University]].<ref name="newton_2002"/>

Parzen died in Boca Raton, Florida on February 6, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theeagle.com/news/local/distinguished-a-m-professor-dies-at-age/article_e5dd2f50-1ae0-51b0-b492-e30d21ed7de8.html |title=Distinguished A&M professor dies at age 86 - The Eagle: Local News |publisher=The Eagle |access-date=2016-02-11}}</ref> His son, Michael Parzen, is a Senior Lecturer of Statistics at [[Harvard University]].
